deepdive.sec: Integrated Mining & Critical Minerals (Iron Ore, Steel, Copper/Cobalt)

bull_bear.body: Debt reduction: Redeeming Thriveni RPS (INR 700 Cr paid April 2026, remaining INR 2,100 Cr over 3 years). Reinvestment: Heavy capex into vertical integration (Steel, BHQ) and critical minerals (DRC). Potential future IPO for Thriveni subsidiary to unlock value, though not immediate.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical/Operational Risk: DRC operations (mitigated by US strategic partnership); Execution Risk: BHQ plant commissioning by Dec 2027; Commodity Price Volatility: Iron ore/pellet realization sensitivity; Regulatory: Royalty changes on low-grade ore (managed via beneficiation).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, execution-focused, and visionary. Emphasizes 'structural' margin improvements over cyclical gains. Strong emphasis on strategic alignment with US critical mineral goals to de-risk DRC exposure. Celebratory of market cap milestone (INR 1 Lakh Cr).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The US-DRC critical mineral agreement (Dec 2025) is a key de-risking factor for their Congo assets, positioning Lloyds as a non-Chinese alternative for US supply chains. The take-or-pay nature of the Tata Steel pipeline asset generates disproportionate free cash flow relative to sustaining capex. BHQ beneficiation not just a volume play but a significant royalty tax arbitrage.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "All the expansion plans are drawn with the most efficient capital allocation"; the deck cites FY26 average RoCE of 56% (ex CWIP) and average RoE of 37%.
- IPS (capital subsidy): entitled to receive refund of State GST and royalty on captive ore consumed.
- Consolidated net D/E moved from -0.17 (FY23), -0.10 (FY24), 0.00 (FY25) to 1.20 (FY26) as the capex cycle was funded; standalone net debt as on 30.06.2026 stated at INR 56,161 mn, and TEIPL net debt (incl RPS) as on 30.06.26 at INR 58,205 mn.
- Renewable SPV structure chosen for capital efficiency: "Exposure is limited to a minority equity stake, not full project capital expenditure", with captive tariff fixed for 25 years insulating from DISCOM tariff revisions and exemption from cross-subsidy and additional surcharge; stated savings of INR ~620 Mn in year 1 and INR ~14.5 Bn over 25 years by SPV.
- Consolidated networth rose from 15,290 (FY23) to 28,108 (FY24) to 64,601 (FY25) to 1,42,661 INR Mn (FY26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Iron Ore: Production 22MT (+120% YoY), Sales 16.18MT, Realization INR 5,806/ton, EBITDA/ton INR 1,930. Pellets: 3.03MT produced in FY26 (ramped to 100% utilization in 4 months), Realization INR 9,590/ton, EBITDA/ton INR 4,040. DRI: 480k tons (+56% YoY), Realization INR 27,306/ton. Thriveni (Coal/Iron): EBITDA INR 1,990 Cr (+87% YoY), Margin 25%. Copper (DRC): 700-750 tons produced in Q4, targeting 9-10k tons in FY27 from Surya; CHEMAF to contribute from July 2027.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain diversification away from China for critical minerals | US Defense & EV OEMs | beneficiary | High | Lloyds' DRC assets (Surya/CHEMAF) are explicitly framed as a flagship project under the new US-DRC critical mineral pact, offering a secure, non-Chinese source of copper/cobalt. |
| High logistics costs in Indian steel production | Tata Steel | beneficiary | High | Beneficiary of the dedicated, cost-efficient slurry pipeline near Kalinganagar, securing stable iron ore/pellet supply with reduced transport costs. |
| Margin compression in low-grade iron ore mining | Competitors without beneficiation tech | loser | Med | Lloyds' BHQ plant allows profitable processing of low-grade ore (royalty arbitrage), potentially squeezing out players reliant on high-grade reserves or lacking beneficiation tech. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "LMEL is building world-class assets in steel manufacturing, revolutionising iron ore mining and beneficiation, aligning with the nation's steel production goals" at Chandrapur & Gadchiroli, Maharashtra.
- Allocated (captive) iron ore mine "thereby saving outflow on premium royalty"; mine lease valid till CY2057, which the deck argues makes LMEL "one of the prominent miners beyond CY30" as more than 80 MTPA of iron ore capacity comes up for auction till CY30 at high auction premiums (2026 average premium 126.00% of IBM notified prices).
- Stated iron ore reserves: DSO 157 mnt and BHQ 706 mnt; the company describes itself as forward integrating into 12 mnt pellet and 4.2 mnt steelmaking.
- Surjagarh Iron Ore Mine (SIOM) is described as "strategically located in the centre of India, equidistant from most steel plants", supporting a "Door-To-Door Delivery" service promise.
- Deck claims India's first integrated green pellet chain.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Tata Steel / BRPL] Tata Steel - Lloyds Metals MoU to explore strategic collaboration across mining, logistics and steel manufacturing; BRPL began MDO operations at Tata Steel's Joda West manganese mines on 1 June 2026 (Q1FY27 EBITDA INR ~48 Cr, pellet production 540 KTPA) and a feasibility study for a slurry pipeline linking Tata Steel's Odisha mines to its steel plants is under discussion, to be developed by BRPL under a BOT service model.
- [Panguna, via Thriveni/associate] Mining lease commencement with the ABG on 7 August; 400+ people employed with 1,200+ engaged; Learning & Development Centre inaugurated 11 July with 300 cadets; hospital construction to complete in 6 months; exploration drilling started to validate historical geology.
- [Geomysore gold] Described as India's first private integrated gold mining and processing company; plant inaugurated by the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on 24 July 2026; Q1 production of ROM 0.17 MT and exploration/drilling of 14,105 mtr.
- [Copper loss driver] Q1FY27 copper EBITDA was negative $2.63 mn, which the deck attributes to the closure of EP1 (lower revenue), higher sulphuric acid and diesel prices "due to middle east war", and continuing employee and operating costs during the transition.
- [Thriveni coal recognition] Thriveni Sainik Mining PB West and PB North West achieved a 5-Star Rating from the Ministry of Coal (FY2024-25) and retained the No. 1 position among all opencast coal mines in India for a 2nd consecutive year.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin sustained at ~34% due to value-added mix shift (32% of revenue vs 20% prior) and operational leverage. Cost deflation: Slurry pipeline and EV/LNG mining fleet driving INR 2,000 Cr annualized savings by FY28. BHQ project expected to further reduce cost base via royalty arbitrage on lower-grade feed.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Topline to scale with volume (Iron ore dispatch 27MT, Pellets 7.75-8MT in FY27); Margin: Structural sustainment >30% aided by INR 2,000 Cr annualized cost savings by FY28; Order Inflow: New mining leases in Odisha/Jharkhand commencing FY27; Capex/Commissioning: FY27 capex ~INR 15,000 Cr consolidated (INR 10,500 Cr standalone + INR 2,000 Cr Copper + Thriveni); Wire rod mill commissioning late FY26; BHQ plant phase-1 ready by Dec 2027.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Production-driven model; Key contractual anchor: Take-or-pay slurry pipeline agreement with Tata Steel ensuring high free cash flow conversion; Mining lease expansions in Gadchiroli (55MT capacity) and new Odisha/Jharkhand mines targeting 35MT+ iron ore volume in FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: BHQ Beneficiation Plant (Dec 2027): Converts low-grade ore to 66-67% grade, reducing royalty costs and boosting EBITDA/ton by INR 700-800. Steel Integration: 1.2MT wire rod mill commissioning late FY26. Critical Minerals: Pathway to 100k tons copper capacity over 3-5 years via CHEMAF/Surya. Logistics: Second slurry pipeline (Hedri-Ghugus) to save INR 500/ton on 16MT volume.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Lloyds Metals executed a historic scale-up in FY26 with iron ore production doubling to 22MT and pellet capacity hitting 8MT, driving standalone EBITDA margins to ~34% via structural logistics savings. The strategic pivot into critical minerals via DRC copper/cobalt assets (Surya + CHEMAF) and the impending BHQ beneficiation plant position the company as a diversified energy-transition play beyond traditional steel inputs.

open.item: Consolidated capex outlay ~INR14,000 crores over this year and next; ~INR6,000 cr from debt, balance internal accruals; 9M standalone capex ~INR4,236 cr.
MDO consolidation to add ~10-15% (roughly INR350-500 per ton) to Lloyds' mining margins.
MDO cost to fall ~INR150-200/ton after enhanced mining stabilizes, another ~INR150-200/ton from beneficiation, and slurry pipeline to cut transport cost ~INR600/ton.
~INR900 crores pending from warrants expected in March (around 15-18 March).
FY26 captive consumption ~8 mt for pellet plants plus ~1-1.2 mt for DRI, leaving ~18 mt for open-market iron ore.
Planning ~INR9,500 crore NCD issue over next 6 months plus ~INR800 cr working capital sanctioned; targeting debt/EBITDA of ~1x; FY27 consol debt ~INR8,000 cr.
3 mt integrated steel plant (flat/value-added products) construction work to start mid-to-end FY27; land under acquisition, project mix being restudied.
FY27 guidance: iron ore production 26 mt, dispatches 27 mt, pellet 7.75-8 mt, DRI 825,000 tons, plus formal steelmaking entry with ~150,000 tons wire rod.
1.2 million ton wire rod mill (blast furnace, arc furnace, coke oven, rolling mill) to be commissioned in the last quarter of FY27.

Total remaining capex ~INR14,500 cr over 2 years; FY27 standalone ~INR10,000-11,000 cr (incl BHQ, Chandrapur ISP), ~INR12,500 cr+ FY28; consolidated FY27 ~INR15,000 cr incl copper (~INR2,000 cr) and Thriveni (~INR1,000 cr).
Surya plant ~85-90% complete; total plant capex ~$1.1bn ($800m+ spent), needing ~$200-260m more; CHEMAF ~$200m additional (non-recourse to LMEL).
Pellet debottlenecking permissions targeted by FY27 year-end to lift both plants toward 10 mt combined capacity.
Thriveni Odisha volumes to grow ~39% YoY to 34-35 mt in FY27 with new mines (Dalpahar 3 mt, Lasarda-Pacheri 1.5 mt from Q1 FY27) and capacity enhancements.
Thriveni FY27 volume growth >75% at Surjagarh (incl. BHQ); total Thriveni EBITDA nearly doubled YoY to INR1,990 cr in FY26 (25% margin).
Pellet capacity to grow from 0 last year to 9.5 mt now and 13.5 mt next year.
BHQ beneficiation first phase (30 mt input / ~12 mt output) targeted ready by December 2027; major machines ordered from a key European supplier.
BHQ beneficiation plant (first phase) to be commissioned by December '27; land procurement under control, engineering and ordering complete (FLSmidth).
FY28: 1.2 mt steel plant to run at ~75-80% (~1 mt production); pellet plant at 8-9 mt; no further iron ore volume increase (maxed at EC).
Annual cost savings to surpass INR2,000 crores per annum as logistics/sustainability initiatives mature by March '28.
Consol net debt ~INR7,100 cr at Dec'25, not to exceed that for FY26; peak debt in FY28 at ~INR10,500-10,600 cr, targeting ~1x debt/EBITDA.
